description: Convergence Widget — a compact dashboard widget that visualizes how the verification-agentic loop is converging (or not) across iterations. Displayed on the active dashboard during workflow runs, it provides real-time visual feedback on whether the AI is making progress fixing verification failures. Shows a mini bar chart of failed step counts per iteration, a trend indicator (Improving/Stalled/Regressing), and a summary line with delta information. Data arrives via the Tauri 'iteration-metrics' event emitted by EventBroadcaster after each verification phase. The widget resets when the active task run changes. The related 'blame-attribution' event provides complementary data about which iterations caused which failures, enabling future integration of oscillation/blame overlays onto the convergence chart.

groups.name: Widget Identity and Visibility
groups.description: The Convergence widget appears on the active dashboard when a workflow run is in progress and has completed at least one verification iteration. It should be immediately recognizable as a convergence monitor and not confused with other metric widgets. The widget renders nothing (returns null) when no metrics have been received yet, avoiding visual noise before the first iteration completes.

assertions.description: The widget displays a 'Convergence' heading so users can identify its purpose among other dashboard widgets
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received for the current task run

assertions.description: The widget is not rendered until the first iteration-metrics event arrives, preventing a confusing empty chart from appearing before any verification has occurred
assertions.precondition: No iteration-metrics events have been received yet (e.g., the run is still in its setup or first agentic phase)

groups.name: Trend Indicator
groups.description: The trend indicator shows the current convergence direction based on the latest two iterations. It uses a color-coded icon and label: green TrendingDown arrow for 'Improving' (fewer failures than previous iteration), amber Minus for 'Stalled' (same failure count or isStalled flag), red TrendingUp arrow for 'Regressing' (more failures than previous iteration). The trend is the most important at-a-glance signal — it tells the user whether to keep waiting or intervene.

assertions.description: When the latest iteration has fewer failed steps than the previous iteration, the trend shows 'Improving' with a green downward arrow, signaling the AI is making progress
assertions.precondition: At least 2 iterations have been received, and latest.failedStepCount < previous.failedStepCount

assertions.description: When the latest iteration has the same failure count as the previous iteration or isStalled is true, the trend shows 'Stalled' with an amber dash, warning the user that progress has stopped
assertions.precondition: At least 2 iterations have been received, and latest.failedStepCount == previous.failedStepCount or latest.isStalled == true

assertions.description: When the latest iteration has more failed steps than the previous iteration, the trend shows 'Regressing' with a red upward arrow, alerting the user that the AI's changes are making things worse
assertions.precondition: At least 2 iterations have been received, and latest.failedStepCount > previous.failedStepCount

assertions.description: When the latest iteration is stalled (isStalled flag from convergence detector), an amber AlertTriangle icon appears next to the heading as an additional visual warning
assertions.precondition: latest.isStalled == true

groups.name: Mini Bar Chart
groups.description: A CSS-based bar chart showing failed step counts per iteration. Each bar represents one iteration, with height proportional to the number of failed steps (minimum 2px, maximum 80px, scaled to the highest failure count). Bar colors encode the change direction: green (bg-emerald-500) for zero failures, amber (bg-amber-500) for no change or improvement, red (bg-red-500) for regression. The chart displays the last 20 iterations (MAX_VISIBLE_ITERATIONS) and scrolls horizontally if more exist. Each bar has a tooltip showing 'Iteration N: X failed, Y passed'.

assertions.description: Each iteration that has been received renders as a vertical bar in the chart, with the iteration number displayed below it
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received

assertions.description: When an iteration has zero failed steps, its bar is green (bg-emerald-500), visually communicating complete success
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has failedStepCount == 0
assertions.expected: The bar for that iteration is green

assertions.description: When an iteration has more failures than the previous iteration, its bar is red (bg-red-500), drawing attention to regressions
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration has more failures than its predecessor
assertions.expected: The bar for that iteration is red

assertions.description: Hovering over a bar shows a tooltip with the exact counts: 'Iteration N: X failed, Y passed'
assertions.precondition: User hovers over a bar in the chart

assertions.description: The chart displays at most 20 iterations (MAX_VISIBLE_ITERATIONS constant). When more iterations exist, only the most recent 20 are shown, with horizontal scroll available for viewing
assertions.precondition: More than 20 iterations have been received

groups.name: Summary Text and Counts
groups.description: Below the bar chart, a summary text line and pass/fail counts provide precise numbers for the latest iteration. The summary includes the current iteration number, the number of failing steps, the delta from the previous iteration (e.g., 'down 2 from 5'), and counts of new vs repeated failures. The pass/fail/skipped counts below use color coding: green for passed, red for failed, grey for skipped.

assertions.description: The summary shows the current iteration number so users know how many iterations have elapsed
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received

assertions.description: The summary shows how many steps are currently failing
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received

assertions.description: When there are 2+ iterations, the summary shows the change from the previous iteration (e.g., 'down 2 from 5' or 'up 1 from 3'), giving users immediate delta context
assertions.precondition: At least 2 iterations have been received and the failure count changed between them

assertions.description: The passed step count is shown in green, giving users a precise number alongside the visual chart
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received

assertions.description: The failed step count is shown in red
assertions.precondition: At least one iteration-metrics event has been received

assertions.description: The skipped step count is shown in grey only when there are skipped steps, avoiding noise when all steps ran
assertions.precondition: latest.skippedStepCount > 0

groups.name: Real-Time Event Handling
groups.description: The widget subscribes to the Tauri 'iteration-metrics' event via @tauri-apps/api/event.listen(). Each event payload contains task_run_id, iteration, failed_step_count, passed_step_count, skipped_step_count, new_failures, repeated_failures, and is_stalled. The widget filters events to only the current task run (from useCurrentTaskRunId context) and appends new metrics to its state array. When the task run changes, the metrics array is reset to empty. The event is emitted by EventBroadcaster::iteration_metrics() in handle_evaluate_verification() after each verification phase completes.

assertions.description: Each new iteration-metrics event adds a bar to the chart without discarding previous bars, so users see the full convergence history build up in real-time
assertions.precondition: Multiple iteration-metrics events have been received for the current task run
assertions.expected: All received iterations are visible as bars in the chart

assertions.description: When the active task run changes (e.g., user switches to a different run), the metrics array resets and the chart starts fresh, avoiding cross-run data contamination
assertions.precondition: User switched to a different task run that has not yet emitted any iteration-metrics events
assertions.expected: Widget is hidden (returns null) until the new run's first iteration completes

assertions.description: Events from other task runs (concurrent runs) are ignored — only events matching the current useCurrentTaskRunId are processed
assertions.precondition: Multiple task runs are active simultaneously
assertions.expected: Only iterations from the currently selected task run appear in the chart

groups.name: Blame Attribution Integration
groups.description: The convergence widget currently tracks iteration-metrics events only. The blame engine emits a complementary 'blame-attribution' event with the same task_run_id and iteration number. A future enhancement could overlay blame signals onto the convergence chart — for example, marking bars with an oscillation icon when the blame engine detects file oscillation, or coloring bars differently when the escalation policy's rethink prompt is injected. This group documents the architectural connection between the convergence widget and the blame system.

assertions.description: The 'blame-attribution' Tauri event is emitted alongside 'iteration-metrics' for the same task_run_id and iteration, making it available for the widget to consume without additional API calls
assertions.precondition: A verification iteration completed with failures and the blame engine produced attributions
assertions.notes: Documents architectural availability. The convergence widget does not yet subscribe to blame-attribution events. Both events share task_run_id and iteration fields for correlation.

assertions.description: When the blame engine detects file oscillation (3+ consecutive iterations modifying the same file), the convergence chart could annotate the relevant bars with an oscillation indicator, making the stuck-loop pattern visible in the chart itself rather than requiring navigation to the Blame tab
assertions.precondition: blame-attribution event received with oscillating_files > 0
assertions.notes: Future enhancement. Oscillation detection data is available via the blame-attribution event's oscillating_files count and the full blame_json payload.

states.name: Hidden — No Metrics Received
states.description: No iteration-metrics events have been received for the current task run. The widget renders nothing (returns null), so neither the heading nor the chart are present in the DOM.

transitions.name: First iteration-metrics event arrives for the current task run

states.name: Single Iteration — First Data Point
states.description: Exactly one iteration-metrics event has been received. The widget is visible with the Convergence heading, a single bar in the chart, the iteration number and failing count in the summary, and pass/fail counts. No trend indicator or delta text is shown because there is no previous iteration to compare against.

transitions.name: Second iteration arrives with fewer failures than the first
Second iteration arrives with same failure count or isStalled flag
Second iteration arrives with more failures than the first
Active task run changes to a run with no metrics yet

states.name: Improving — Failures Decreasing
states.description: Two or more iterations received, and the latest iteration has fewer failed steps than the previous. The trend indicator shows 'Improving' with a green TrendingDown arrow. The summary includes a delta line (e.g., 'down 2 from 5'). The bar chart shows all received iterations with color-coded bars.

transitions.name: Next iteration arrives with same failure count or isStalled flag
Next iteration arrives with more failures
Active task run changes to a run with no metrics yet

states.name: Stalled — No Progress
states.description: Two or more iterations received, and the latest iteration has the same failure count as the previous or the isStalled flag is true. The trend indicator shows 'Stalled' with an amber Minus icon. An amber AlertTriangle icon appears next to the heading when isStalled is true. The summary shows the current counts without a delta or with a zero delta.

transitions.name: Next iteration arrives with fewer failures
Next iteration arrives with more failures
Active task run changes to a run with no metrics yet

states.name: Regressing — Failures Increasing
states.description: Two or more iterations received, and the latest iteration has more failed steps than the previous. The trend indicator shows 'Regressing' with a red TrendingUp arrow. The summary includes a delta line (e.g., 'up 1 from 3'). Red bars appear in the chart for regressing iterations.

transitions.name: Next iteration arrives with fewer failures
Next iteration arrives with same failure count or isStalled flag
Active task run changes to a run with no metrics yet

Tauri Event: blame-attribution -> { task_run_id, iteration, attributed_failures, oscillating_files, revert_patterns, blame_json }
